flashcards.a: $0.44/DPU-hour on-demand, billed per-second with a 1-minute minimum; $0.29/DPU-hour under Flex execution for jobs that can tolerate a delayed start.

flashcards.q: Give three concrete reasons Glue can be worse than EMR for a job.
flashcards.a: Long-running/continuous jobs (Glue's per-job startup overhead repeats each run), need for custom Spark config/libraries/versions, and poorly-optimized Spark code that can burn 10x the DPU-hours a tuned EMR job would.

flashcards.q: Athena pricing model and minimum charge?
flashcards.a: $5 per TB of data scanned, with a 10MB minimum charge per query. It's managed Presto/Trino under the hood.

flashcards.q: What are the three cost levers for Athena, in order of typical impact?
flashcards.a: 1) Columnar format (Parquet/ORC -- read only referenced columns) 2) Compression (Snappy 3-5x, gzip 5-10x) 3) Partitioning on a filtered column (e.g. date). A documented case went from ~15TB/query to ~50GB/query using all three.

flashcards.q: What is partition projection and why use it over registered partitions?
flashcards.a: Athena computes partition S3 locations algorithmically from a configured pattern (date range, enum list) instead of storing every partition in the Glue Catalog -- eliminates crawler/MSCK REPAIR maintenance and per-query metadata lookup overhead for high-cardinality time-series tables.

flashcards.q: What does Redshift RA3 change architecturally?
flashcards.a: Decouples compute from storage via Redshift Managed Storage -- storage scales independently up to 64TB/node, so you size compute for query performance rather than data volume.

DISTKEY determines which node a row physically lands on (colocate joined tables to avoid cross-node shuffle). SORTKEY determines on-disk ordering within a node, enabling zone-map block skipping on range-filtered queries.

flashcards.q: What's the fundamental billing-model difference between Redshift and Athena/BigQuery?
flashcards.a: Redshift (outside Serverless) is cluster-billed -- you pay for provisioned compute-time whether idle or not. Athena/BigQuery are query-billed -- you pay per byte scanned, nothing when idle. This flips the cost-optimization approach from 'size the cluster' to 'control the scan'.

flashcards.q: Kinesis Data Streams shard throughput limit?
flashcards.a: 1 MB/s in, 2 MB/s out per shard in provisioned mode. To match a 1GB/s Kafka topic on 10 partitions you'd need on the order of 1,000 provisioned-mode Kinesis shards.

flashcards.q: Kinesis Data Streams vs Firehose vs MSK -- one-line selection rule for each?
flashcards.a: Data Streams: need custom multi-consumer processing or replay. Firehose: lowest-effort delivery pipe into S3/Parquet, no consumer code, but one-way (not replayable). MSK: already have Kafka clients/tooling -- migration cost of rewriting almost never pays off.

flashcards.q: When is OpenSearch the wrong tool for a RAG retrieval backend?
flashcards.a: When the workload is pure vector-similarity search with no lexical/full-text need and the team wants minimal index-tuning ops -- a dedicated vector DB or Bedrock Knowledge Bases with a simpler backend gives comparable retrieval quality with less cluster/shard management. OpenSearch earns its complexity for hybrid BM25+vector search.

flashcards.q: What does Redshift Spectrum do, and what does it NOT do?
flashcards.a: Lets a Redshift cluster query data sitting in S3 directly without loading it. It does NOT add to the cluster's managed storage, since the queried data never actually lands in Redshift.

flashcards.q: What is the Glue Data Catalog's role beyond Glue ETL jobs?
flashcards.a: A shared, Hive-metastore-compatible metadata store used automatically by Athena, Redshift Spectrum, and EMR -- one schema/partition registry serving multiple query engines, which is often the real reason to use Glue even without running a Glue ETL job.
